title: Spartak make history: Subotica club crowned Serbian champions for the first time
description: Spartak Office Shoes are champions of Serbia for the first time in their history, edging FMP 76-73 in an overtime thriller to complete one of the most remarkable runs in the modern Serbian game a title series featuring neither Crvena Zvezda nor Partizan. The Subotica side, who had already stunned Crvena Zvezda in the semifinals, kept their nerve in a tense, see-sawing final. Spartak controlled the early going, leading 24-19 after the first quarter and pushing the advantage through a strong third (22-16) to take command. But FMP refused to fold, storming back with an 18-5 fourth quarter to force overtime at 68-68. In the extra period, Spartak outscored FMP 8-5 to seal the historic championship.
imageCaption: Spartak Subotica clinch historic first title in Serbia (Photo: KK Spartak)

title: Partizan sweep Spartak to lift KLS title
description: Spartak - Partizan 79-93 Partizan claimed KLS title. They outgunned Spartak Subotica on the road to complete the sweep of the championship series. The guests trailed by 5 points after first quarter, but they stormed back to get the 1-point lead at the halftime and eventually won the game 93-79. Partizan made 24-of-27 free shots (88.9 percent) during the game. American guard Duane Washington Jr (190-2000, college: Ohio St.) scored 41 points (!!!), 8 rebounds and 4 assists to lead the charge for the winners and Canadian forward Isiaha Mike (201-1997, college: SMU) chipped in 15 points during the contest. Four Partizan players scored in double figures. Forward Luka Cerovina (201-2000) responded with 22 points and 4 assists and the former international center Dusan Miletic (213-1998) scored 21 points and 5 rebounds (on 7-of-9 shooting from the field). Both coaches used bench players which…
imageCaption: Partizan sweep Spartak to lift KLS title (Photo: kls.rs)

title: Crvena Zvezda wins Serbian league after finals Game 2 suspension
description: Crvena Zvezda finished the season by winning a third title after the Serbian Cup and the ABA League, by prevailing 20-0 in Game 2 of the Serbian League finals. With hosts Partizan leading 57-45, the game was interrupted due to insulting chants by Partizan fans toward the president of Zvezda, Nebojsa Covic . Then objects were thrown on the court and Zvezda players went to the lockers, followed by Partizan and the referees. The arena was evacuated, however, the game was not continued on time and ultimately Zvezda won the game 20-0 with Partizanâ€™s side being held responsible for the interruption and their players never returning to court. The league is expected to ratify the decision in a few hours. The Serbian league is the fourth competition, both in number and importance, for Zvezda and Partizan after the EuroLeague, the regional Adriatic League, which is practically their domestic…

title: Crvena zvezda celebrate KLS title
description: FMP - Crvena zvezda 72-82 Crvena zvezda earned the eighth straight KLS title. They overcame FMP on the road today to complete the sweep of the championship series. Luka Mitrovic (204-C-1993, agency: Octagon Europe) scored 16 points to pace the visitors. He was named the Finals MVP. FMP got to a quick start. They unloaded 27 points in the first period to take a 4-point lead. But Crvena zvezda responded with a 20-9 run in the second stanza to ensure a 43-36 halftime lead. FMP narrowed the distance to just 6 points heading into the fourth stanza. But Crvena zvezda controlled the tempo in the final period. They boosted the margin to double digits and eased to the decisive victory at the end. title: Crvena Zvezda top FMP to clinch KLS title
description: FMP - Crvena Zvezda 59-71 Crvena Zvezda clinched KLS title. They overcame KK FMP Meridian on the road to complete the sweep of the championship series. Nikola Ivanovic (190-G-1994, agency: BeoBasket) came off the bench to topscore with 21 points. Crvena Zvezda limited their opponents to just 9 points in the first period to open a 6-point lead. FMP increased the tempo in the second frame. They sank 22 points in the second period to narrow the deficit at 3-point mark 31-34. Crvena Zvezda however came off the locker room swinging. They poured in 25 points to ensure a 14-point lead. FMP slowed their opponents down in the fourth period but could not avoid the loss. Nikola Kalinic (203-F-1991) tossed in 12 points for the winning side. Marko Radonjic (191-PG-1993) answered with 14 points for FMP. title: Crvena Zvezda are 2020/21 KLS champions
description: Crvena Zvezda - Mega 77-65 Crvena Zvezda celebrated KLS title tonight. They overcame Mega Soccerbet in the decisive third game of the championship series to lift the trophy. The hosts trailed by 3 points after first quarter, but they stormed back to get the 8-point lead at the halftime and eventually won the game 77-65. Strangely Mega outrebounded Crvena Zvezda 32-0 including a 22- advantage in defensive rebounds. It was a great evening for American point guard Langston Hall (193-91, college: Mercer, agency: Octagon Europe) who led his team to a victory scoring 24 points and 4 assists. The former international Ognjen Dobric (200-94, agency: BeoBasket) helped adding 15 points and 9 rebounds. Four Crvena Zvezda players scored in double figures. description: Game 3: Cibona vs Zadar 110-111 2OT With the best-of-three series tied at one apiece, the deciding game 3 was played on Cibona's home court, Dom Sportova, on Saturday, 26 April 1986. Supported by over 10,000 fans, despite plenty of nervy play from the home team (Drazen Petrovic (196-G-1964) getting a technical for accosting the referee and Franjo Arapovic (215-C-1965) getting ejected for striking Darko Pahlic (183-PG-1963)), Cibona had the early lead behind Danko Cvjeticanin (198-SF-1963)'s scoring (got 22 of Cibona's 42 first half points) while Drazen Petrovic, who returned to the squad after controversially sitting out game two, also scored actively. Still, Zadar kept chasing with most of its first half points coming from their twenty-six-year-old captain Veljko Petranovic (204-F/C-1959) and twenty-two-year-old center Stojan Vrankovic (217-C-1964). title: Big controversy: Bosna is a champion despite they were edged in the final game by Sibenka
description: On 9 April 1983, Sibenka and Bosna played the deciding Game 3 of their playoff final series that was decided in the last second. With Bosna up by a point and the clock winding down Sibenka had the last possession, Bosna's Sabit Hadzic was controversially adjudged by the referee Ilija Matijevic to have fouled Sibenka's Drazen Petrovic as he went up for a shot at the buzzer. Since being in the act of shooting, Petrovic got two free throws and proceeded to score both, winning the game and championship for his team. Next morning, the Basketball Federation of Yugoslavia (KSJ) presidency reviewed the game on account the time expired prior to the foul being called and on account of refereeing irregularities.
